ocean: a very large area of sea
The ship sailed across the ocean for nearly two weeks.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
marine: The reserve protects a wide range of marine species.
ecosystems: communities of living things interacting with their environments
Wetlands provide vital ecosystems for many migratory birds.
the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
silent: completely quiet; making or having no sound
The whole audience stayed silent during the final scene of the play.
crisis: a time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger
The company faced a financial crisis after losing its biggest client.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
planetary: relating to a planet or planets
The observatory tracks planetary motion using powerful telescopes.
boundaries: the limits or lines that mark the edge of something
The new fence marks the boundaries between the two properties.
beyond: further away than, or outside the limits of, something
The hiking trail continues far beyond the edge of the forest.
rising: Rising fuel costs pushed up the price of almost everything.
surface: the outer or top layer of something
Dust had settled evenly across the wooden surface of the old table.
temperatures: measures of how hot or cold something is
Temperatures dropped sharply once the sun went down.
chemical: a substance produced by or used in a chemical process
The factory stores several chemicals used in the manufacturing process.
transformation: a complete change in form, appearance, or character
The headline figure captured a genuine transformation, but not the whole of it.
waters: areas of sea or a body of water
A fisherman near Nha Trang has fished the same waters for generations.
poses: presents or causes a risk, problem, or question
The new law poses a challenge for small businesses.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
threat: a statement or sign of intended harm, or a source of danger
The serious threat is the format.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
food: any substance eaten to maintain life and growth
They stored enough food to last through the winter.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
atmospheric: relating to the atmosphere or the air around us
Atmospheric pressure drops sharply as you climb a tall mountain.
warming: the process of becoming warmer, especially the climate
Local fixes do not reverse a warming climate on their own.
captures: obtains or secures a share of something; records accurately
The company captures most of the profit from the new invention.
public: provided by the state for everyone; open to all people
The new library is open to the public every day of the week.
discourse: communication or debate about a topic, spoken or written
Climate change has become a central topic in public discourse.
companion: accompanying or paired with something else
The museum published a companion guide to accompany its new exhibition.
equal: the same in size, amount, value, or status
Both teams scored an equal number of points by half-time.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
silently: The cat crept silently across the floor toward the sleeping bird.
beneath: in or to a lower position than something
A small stream flowed quietly beneath the old wooden footbridge.
waves: A reef breaks waves before they reach the beach, reducing storm damage.
since: from a particular time in the past until now, or because
He has lived in this city since he graduated from university.
industrial: The town grew rapidly after a new industrial park opened.
revolution: a dramatic and wide-reaching change in conditions or ideas
cuộc cách mạng, sự thay đổi lớn
The digital revolution transformed how people communicate worldwide.
oceans: very large areas of sea; plural of ocean
Plastic waste has been found even in the deepest oceans.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
served: provided someone with food, service, or help
The soup was served hot, straight from the pot.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
carbon: a chemical element found in all living things and fossil fuels
The factory aims to cut its carbon output by half this decade.
sink: to go down below the surface of something, especially a liquid or soft material
The old boat began to sink slowly after hitting the rocks.
absorbing: taking in or soaking up something gradually
The sponge kept absorbing water until it could hold no more.
approximately: close to a particular number or amount; roughly
The journey takes approximately three hours by train from the city.
thirty: My grandmother has lived in this house for thirty years.
percent: one part in every hundred; a proportion out of 100
Nearly sixty percent of residents voted in favor of the new park.
emissions: substances, especially gases, released into the air
The city introduced rules to cut vehicle emissions sharply.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
colossal: extremely large in size or extent
A colossal wave crashed over the harbor wall during the storm.
capacity: the ability to do, hold, or produce something
The factory's production capacity doubled after the new machines arrived.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
life: the state of being alive, or the period from birth to death
She moved to the countryside to enjoy a quieter life.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance
This plan works far better than the last one did.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
thermal: relating to heat, or designed to keep in heat
She wore thermal socks to keep her feet warm on the hike.
yet: The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
come: to move toward or arrive at a particular place; to originate from
Most of the fruit here comes from small family farms.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
cost: the amount of money needed to buy, do, or produce something
The cost of the renovation was far higher than the family expected.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
seawater: The plant can filter seawater into drinkable fresh water.
forms: different types, shapes, or versions of something
Renewable energy comes in many forms, from solar to wind.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
ions: atoms or molecules with an electric charge, having gained or lost electrons
Salt dissolves in water into positive and negative ions.
hydrogen: a light, colourless gas, the simplest chemical element
Engineers are testing hydrogen as a clean fuel for buses.
resulting: happening as a consequence of something
Heavy rain caused flooding, and the resulting damage was severe.
proliferation: a rapid increase in the number or spread of something
sự gia tăng nhanh chóng, sự lan rộng
The proliferation of cheap goods changed local trade patterns.
free: not fixed or restricted; able to move or act as desired
tự do, không bị ràng buộc
Engineers left a small gap so the metal is free to expand.
driving: operating a vehicle, or providing power or force to something
A single large engine was responsible for driving all the machines in the factory.
phenomenon: a fact or event, especially one that is unusual
Lightning is a natural phenomenon that has fascinated humans for centuries.
designated: officially chosen or named for a particular purpose
UNESCO designated the old town as a World Heritage Site.
crucially: in a way that is extremely important, especially to an outcome
The plan worked because, crucially, everyone understood their role.
these: used to refer to people or things nearby or just mentioned
These shoes are far more comfortable than my old ones.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
drastically: in a way that is sudden and extreme
một cách mạnh mẽ, đột ngột
Sales dropped drastically after the factory closed down.
fundamental: forming a necessary base or core; basic and important
Clean water is a fundamental need for every community.
building: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or office
The old building was renovated into modern apartments last year.
blocks: to stop something from passing or happening
A fallen tree blocks the main road after last night's storm.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
organisms: individual living things; plural of organism
Scientists discovered several new organisms living near the deep-sea vents.
microscopic: so small it can only be seen with a microscope
The lab identified microscopic traces of the chemical in the water supply.
base: the main group of supporters or customers of something; also the bottom part
The company built a loyal customer base over two decades.
vast: extremely large in area, size or amount
The desert stretches across a vast area of the continent.
coral: a hard, often colourful substance formed by tiny sea animals
Divers photographed a vast coral reef teeming with colourful fish.
reef: a ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the sea
Divers explored the colourful reef just off the coast.
quarter: one of four equal parts of something
He spends roughly a quarter of his salary on rent each month.
all: the whole quantity or extent of something
She spent all summer preparing for the entrance exam.
species: a group of living things that can breed together and share characteristics
Scientists discovered a new species of frog in the rainforest.
calcium: a chemical element found in bones, shells, and rock
The coral secretes calcium to build its hard outer skeleton.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
literally: in a literal sense; word for word
The phrase literally means 'silk road' in German.
exhibit: an object or collection displayed for the public to view
A Van Gogh exhibit has been travelling through several cities.
settlement: a place where people establish a community; an official agreement
Archaeologists uncovered a small settlement dating back centuries.
rates: speeds at which things happen, or fixed prices or measures
Interest rates rose sharply after the central bank's announcement.
fish: a cold-blooded animal that lives in water and breathes through gills
They caught several fish in the river yesterday.
suffer: to experience something unpleasant, such as pain or loss
Farmers suffer most when the rains fail two years running.
chemistry: the branch of science dealing with substances, or the composition of a substance
hoá học, thành phần hoá học
She studied chemistry at university before becoming a pharmacist.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
begins: The film begins with a dramatic scene in the mountains.
subtle: not obvious or easy to notice; delicate
There was a subtle change in her tone during the interview.
ultimately: in the end; finally, after everything else has been considered
It ultimately depends on the manager and how well you negotiate with them.
ecological: relating to the relationship between living things and their environment
The dam's construction raised serious ecological concerns.
through: moving in one side and out the other; by means of
Brick, asphalt and concrete absorb heat all day and release it slowly through the night.
global: relating to the whole world; worldwide

fisheries: areas or industries concerned with catching fish
